learning.title: A walk of an untrusted checkout must refuse any name containing U+FFFD
learning.trigger: Code walks a candidate checkout with `Deno.readDir` to find or remove symlinks, or otherwise acts on names it read from untrusted git content.
learning.mistake: `Deno.readDir` decodes a file name that is not valid UTF-8 lossily, replacing each bad byte with U+FFFD. Two distinct names can then read as the same string. A decoy file really named with U+FFFD keeps an escaping symlink beside it from being found: the walk acts on the decoy and never on the link. Without a decoy the walk throws and every retry fails the same way. Reproduced with a real worktree checkout, not a mock.
learning.rule: Refuse the whole checkout before any model or tool starts when any entry name contains U+FFFD, with a non-retryable fault (`REVIEWER_CHECKOUT_UNSAFE`, 422), and say so in the operator docs. Do not try to repair or skip such a name. Unlink links that leave the tree as the link itself, never its target, and compare `git status` before and after the run.

verification.requirement: A non-UTF-8 name beside a U+FFFD decoy, a lone non-UTF-8 directory and a name that really uses U+FFFD are each refused with the checkout fault and no model starts.

learning.boundary: The candidate then cannot be reviewed at all; the run stops with a `review_failed` decision. That is deliberate: a reviewer that cannot see a candidate safely must not approve it.
